question.problem: Find parametric equations for the normal line to the surface $\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})=1$ at the point $(0,0,\sqrt{e}).$
question.worked_solution:
Let's set $f(x,y,z)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}).$ Then,  our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=1.$ 

A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point $(0,0,\sqrt{e})$ can be found by computing $∇f(0,0,\sqrt{e}).$  

So, we find the gradient and evaluate it at $(0,0,\sqrt{e}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}))i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}))j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}))k \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\text{ }i+\frac{2y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\text{ }j+\frac{2z}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\text{ }k \\ ∇f(0,0,\sqrt{e}) & =\frac{2(0)}{(0)^{2}+(0)^{2}+(\sqrt{e})^{2}}\text{ }i+\frac{2(0)}{(0)^{2}+(0)^{2}+(\sqrt{e})^{2}}\text{ }j+\frac{2\sqrt{e}}{(0)^{2}+(0)^{2}+(\sqrt{e})^{2}}\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{e}}{e}k\end{aligned}
$$

The parametric equations for the normal line to $f(x,y,z)$ at a point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ are given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={x}_{0}+{f}_{x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})t, \\ y & ={y}_{0}+{f}_{y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})t, \\ z & ={z}_{0}+{f}_{z}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametic equations  for the normal line to our surface that  passes through the point $(0,0,\sqrt{e})$ can be written as 
 

$$
x=0,\,y=0,\,z=\sqrt{e}+\frac{2t\sqrt{e}}{e}
$$
